newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Skilled slumps on Optus rollout review.
newsitem.headline: Skilled slumps on Optus rollout review.

text.p: Shares in contract labour firm Skilled Engineering Ltd slumped a further 10 percent or 28 cents to A$2.40 in early Tuesday trade after it warned its profits would slide in the wake of Optus Vision's decision to review its cable rollout.

Skilled said late on Friday it was carrying out five major projects for Optus and would suffer a profit fall of more than 15 percent for the full year to June 30, 1996 because Optus had decided to reschedule or scale back its infrastructure rollout.
Skilled's shares fell 32 cents to A$2.68 on Monday.
"Without giving away any rights the company may have, Skilled advises that its scheduled work has been significantly reduced, affecting sales and profit for this financial year," Skilled said.
By 11.50 a.m. (0150 GMT), volume traded in Skilled Engineering's shares was 29,759.
Brokers said managing director Frank Hargrave's decision to reduce his stake in the company to 39.77 percent from 52.90 percent, as announced on March 20, was also weighing on the stock.
"I would think they'll drop further yet," said Peake Lands Kirwan broker Kevin Lourey.
